source.title: Examining Scaling and Transfer of Language Model Architectures for Machine Translation
source.authors: Biao Zhang; B. Ghorbani; Ankur Bapna; Yong Cheng; Xavier García; Jonathan Shen; O. Firat

record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling behavior in supervised machine translation, an extension of the language-model pretraining scaling claim to translation architectures and task loss.
record.gate_note: The paper measures test log-perplexity while scaling model parameters, fits power-law curves, and reports how scaling patterns differ by architecture and data regime. It also reports scaling against FLOPs and BLEU, but does not test token-count scaling, pretraining loss, extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs, or a compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Cited scaling-law results from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits a Kaplan-style power law with an irreducible-loss term to test log-perplexity against parameters (and FLOPs) for nine supervised MT architectures on three datasets. Its own fits bear on whether power-law scaling holds in another training regime (V5), whether shape matters (V4) and whether exponents depend on setup (V7). It is not LM pretraining, so V1 is not directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that LM architectures scale differently from EncDec, with architectural gaps large at small scale that narrow as parameters grow. They find causal masking and a source LM loss hurt translation, while depth helps more than width. PrefixLM matches EncDec on supervised tasks and beats it on zero-shot by reducing off-target translations. They recommend comparing architectures across the whole scaling curve.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a Kaplan-style fitted power-law form for test PPL, but applies it to supervised machine translation architectures and varies model size through depth or width. It does not test token scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Architecture and parameter-growth method (depth versus width) affect performance; data-limited versus model size-limited regimes differ; evaluation subsets slightly affect fitted exponents. The authors state that exponent variation across evaluation settings is often less than 0.05.

fits_no_version.finding: BLEU rises with parameter count with trends similar to PPL, but the authors call the BLEU-PPL relation non-trivial.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task metrics (BLEU) on the training task track loss scaling only loosely.

record.problems: The reported scaling curves and many values are figure-only; exact fitted exponents are not given in the text. The experiments are supervised translation rather than language-model pretraining, and do not establish small-run extrapolation or compute-optimal allocation. No uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: Model-specific FLOPs curves in Appendix Figures 7 and 13, additional evaluation-subset PPL curves in Figures 8 and 10, and further BLEU curves were not recorded individually; the main textual FLOPs summary is represented by r30, and those omitted plots do not add a separate test of the central loss-scaling versions.

untested.parts: No LM pretraining loss. There is no token-count or data scaling, and no regime free of a data bottleneck for the WMT sweeps.
No extrapolation from small-run fits to much larger runs.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer from pretrained models are not tested. The multilingual and zero-shot experiments report BLEU/PPL against size but fit no power law.
BLEU against params is shown (Fig 2c/d, 14) only as 'similar trends', on the training task itself. There is no downstream-task test and no prediction from loss.
Parameter-counting alternatives, training schedule and fitting-method choices are not tested. Whether curves bend away from a single power law is not tested.

missing.what: Per-architecture fitted exponent p (roughly 0.5–1.0) and irreducible loss L∞ across models and evaluation subsets
Out-of-domain (WMT) fitted scaling curves for Web En-De models, which the authors say follow the same pattern
Scaling against number of layers, where the performance gap also narrows

record.verdict_notes: The fit uses L(N)=α(N0/N)^p+L∞, with N0 taken from a 1-layer EncDec. I moved the rows from V1 to V5 because the loss is supervised translation test PPL, not LM pretraining loss. The WMT sweeps are in a data-limited regime where the authors note overfitting. No uncertainty or fit-quality measures are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests parameter scaling and reports curves against FLOPs, but not token-count scaling. The measure is held-out translation test log-perplexity, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
No separate test of predictions from small-run fits on runs orders of magnitude larger.
Does not search for the loss-minimising parameter/token split at fixed compute or fit either allocation as a function of compute.
Compares depth and width scaling and TopOnly variants, but does not comprehensively vary architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Tests supervised machine translation, not other modalities, repeated-data training, fine-tuning, or transfer from pretrained language models.
Reports translation BLEU against model size, but does not test downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or prediction from pretraining loss.

Shows architecture- and evaluation-setting-related differences in scaling behavior; does not test parameter-counting alternatives, compute-optimal allocation, or whether curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: LM architecture variants (aggregate textual comparison)
rows.size_stated: small through large parameter settings; exact values not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared depth, width, masking, TopOnly encoding, and source-loss variants across model scales.

conditions.value: architectures at small versus large scales

rows.measure: Differences in test-PPL performance across architectures as scale increases
rows.baseline: EncDec reference and other LM variants
rows.value: At small scales, translation-favoring inductive biases perform better; architecture gaps narrow as models grow. CausalLM retains a clear gap in WMT14 En-Fr; the gap is smaller in WMT19 En-Zh, mainly because of overfitting.
rows.note: Aggregate row records the authors' explicit cross-architecture summary; individual plotted scaling curves are recorded separately in r1-r18.
rows.check: This row mixes shape changes (Deep vs Wide at matched params; TopOnly) with different architectures and objectives (CausalLM masking, source LM loss). Only the depth/width and TopOnly comparisons bear on V4. Deep beats Wide at small scale, and the gap 'almost disappears at the end'.

source_check.correct: V4: partial, because shape differences matter at small scales and diminish at larger scales. V7: observed, because architectures and methods of adding parameters show different scaling properties.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state fits V4 but understates the explicitly observed architecture dependence relevant to V7.
